- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., after 85+ values), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not properly captured.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in the first 10 days, then converges or diverges later.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underreacting to sudden drops or spikes in history.
- For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day), model fails to capture the “rebound” or “reversal” phase after a sharp decline, often staying too low.
- Model overconfident in early predictions when history shows high volatility — should adjust for higher uncertainty in volatile periods.
- When history includes a recent peak, model often predicts a sustained high, ignoring potential correction or mean reversion.
